regime.name: linear_gauss_er
regime.description: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, standardized, d 20/50/100, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4; seeds 0-19 attempted, at least 10 per setting run

verdict_rule: D = error(Andrey) - error(bnlearn) per dataset on the datasets both finished; a setting with at least 10 paired datasets is worse when the paired 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs is reported, not judged
fit_protocol: one fit at a time on 1 core, Fisher-z at alpha 0.05 (bnlearn test zf), Gaussian BIC for the score phase, a 600 s wall cap per fit, 1 untimed warm-up fit except at n=5000, mean degree 4, d>=50 (none), 1 timed fit; a capped fit is a timeout, counted as coverage and never scored
error_metric: each entry's own, in its error_metric: the SHD of the output against its own true graph (the moral graph, the skeleton, or the CPDAG), as the median over the paired datasets (the _mean fields hold the means)
complete_definition: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored
seeds_note: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting (10 to 20): 47 seed blocks (seeds 10-19) were skipped by the CPU budget guard before they ran

methods.comparator_setting: bnlearn learn.mb(method='iamb') per variable, joined by the AND rule
methods.error_metric: moral-graph SHD vs the true moral graph; andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means
methods.hardware: AMD EPYC 7713 / AMD EPYC 9534 / Intel Xeon Gold 6542Y nodes (6 hosts), 1 core per fit; Andrey and bnlearn run in the same process slot, so the time ratio pairs, absolute times do not compare across rows
methods.same_graph_test: equal adjacency (moral, skeleton) or equal endpoint marks (CPDAG)

methods.error_metric: skeleton SHD vs the true skeleton; andrey_shd, comparator_shd, and empty_shd are medians over the paired datasets, and the _mean fields their means

methods.note: The setting with 50 variables, 5,000 rows, and mean degree 2 is worse (D +0.50 [+0.05, +1.05]); 16 of its 20 graphs are identical. Most of the gap, +7 pairs of the +10 over its 20 datasets, sits in 2 datasets whose skeletons differ, and the skeleton difference starts at one node's first grow step, where the p-values of several candidates underflow to exactly 0 in bnlearn, which takes the first column among them. Andrey takes the candidate with the strongest test statistic, the association measure of Tsamardinos, Aliferis, and Statnikov (2003). bnlearn's choice, applied in Andrey's search, reproduces bnlearn's skeleton in all 4 traced datasets. The other +3 are orientation differences in 2 datasets with equal skeletons: Meek's rules on a cyclic partially directed graph, and a collider that bnlearn skips for closing a directed cycle.

methods.note: The setting with 100 variables, 1,000 rows, and mean degree 2 is worse (D +0.70 [+0.10, +1.55]); 12 of its 20 graphs are identical. Most of the gap, +12 pairs of the +14 over its 20 datasets, sits in 7 datasets whose skeletons differ, and the skeleton difference starts at one node's first forward step, where the p-values of several candidates underflow to exactly 0 in bnlearn, which takes the first column among them. Andrey takes the candidate with the strongest test statistic, which Tsamardinos, Brown, and Aliferis (2006) use to break ties between equal p-values. bnlearn's choice, applied in Andrey's search, reproduces bnlearn's skeleton in all 8 traced datasets. The other +2 come from one dataset with an equal skeleton, where the two blankets of a triple have equal size and bnlearn tests a collider on one of them, Andrey on both.
